records.title: Housing.
records.description: The text outlines several legislative updates across various legal domains, including zoning, housing, taxation, and property management. Here is a breakdown of key points: 1. **Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs)**: Local agencies can create ADUs and junior ADUs, but this bill prohibits financial fees as part of reasonable restrictions on their development. 2. **Landlord-Tenant Laws**: The bill restricts landlords from charging fees not specified in rental agreements and limits total fees to 5% of the monthly rent. Unauthorized fee charges could result in liability. 3. **Foreclosure Practices**: Mortgage servicers must certify their practices before initiating foreclosure, enhancing borrower protection. 4. **Common Interest Developments**: Updates monetary penalty limits on members and requires opportunities for members to address violations before penalties. 5. **Seismic Retrofitting**: Prioritizes funding for seismic retrofitting of low-income, multifamily housing. 6. **Surplus Land**: Revises the definition of exempt surplus land, especially concerning school districts, aligning it with general surplus property laws. 7. **Housing Planning**: Revises data requirements and revises the allocation methodology process for regional housing needs, increasing collaboration between councils and the Department of Housing. 8. **Public Hearings**: Extends indefinitely the law restricting cities/counties to no more than five hearings for housing projects. 9. **Historic Site Determination**: Extends provisions for determining historic sites for housing projects indefinitely. 10. **Housing Accountability Act**: Extends various provisions indefinitely that limit local agencies from blocking compliant housing projects. 11. **Permit Streamlining Act**: Expands the definition of development projects, extends application processing timelines indefinitely, and removes public notice requirements as preconditions for deemed approvals. 12. **Housing Crisis Act of 2019**: Extends provisions that prevent moratoriums on housing development indefinitely. 13. **Energy Conservation Standards**: Mandates evaluation of energy efficiency measures during standard updates, with a report due by 2030. 14. **California Coastal Act**: Requires the introduction of electronic submissions and exempts specific residential projects from certain appeals. 15. **Tax Credits for Renters**: Proposes increased tax credits for qualified renters between 2026 and 2031, with refundable credits in excess of tax liability. 16. **Local Program Duties**: Indicates state mandates do not require reimbursement under specified circumstances. These amendments reflect ongoing efforts to streamline housing development processes, enhance tenant rights, support low-income housing initiatives, and modernize existing regulations.

records.title: Regional housing need: methodology: distribution.
records.description: Proposes that units lost during state emergencies be redistributed proportionally across regions, rather than solely replacing them within the affected jurisdictions as a method by the council of governments.

records.title: Transit-oriented housing development: excluded parcels and sites.
records.description: Prohibits transit-oriented housing developments from being built on sites currently used for mobilehome parks, recreational vehicle parks, or special occupancy parks, which are often considered naturally occurring affordable housing.

It shifts the reporting responsibility to HCD.

records.title: Planning and zoning: general plan: judicial challenges.
records.description: Extends the time frame for local governments to comply with court orders related to general plan deficiencies from 60 to 120 days. Requires that when quantified development standards in different plan elements conflict, the most recently adopted element will prevail. Requires HCD to review local agency amendments and mandates that court orders challenging general plans be immediately appealable. Provides more specific guidelines for granting temporary relief during legal challenges and imposes stricter requirements for local governments to address housing element deficiencies.

records.title: Housing Accountability Act: housing development projects.
records.description: Redefines a "housing development project" (where mixed-use developments meant for residential use that are at least 2/3 of the space) to not include hotel, motels or transient lodging. Will apply retroactively to project applications not deemed complete by January 1, 2025, including those submitted before that date.

records.title: Homeless Housing, Assistance, and Prevention program: housing element.
records.description: The Homeless Housing, Assistance, and Prevention (HHAP) program gives grant funding to jurisdictions to improve efforts to address homelessness, with funds allocated across multiple rounds of administration. This bill creates additional requirements for local governments that do not receive HHAP funding: the housing APR must include specific data about the unhoused population and describe key actions the jurisdiction will take to reduce homelessness based on that data

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: environmental leadership development projects: data centers: clean energy powerplant projects.
records.description: Prohibits data center projects from using CEQA categorical exemptions and increases duties of lead agencies to conduct more enviornmental review for data centers. However, the bill also establishes a pathway for data centers to be certified as "environmental leadership development projects" by the Governor (which provides some CEQA related streamlining benefits), provided they meet stringent conditions related to energy use, water conservation, and community benefits, and are overseen by the State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission.

records.title: California Emergency Services Act: disaster recovery: wildfires.
records.description: Requires HCD coordinate with local gov'ts to establish rapid permitting processes for rebuilding destroyed or damaged residential properties.

records.title: Residential windows: retrofitting: California Energy Code compliance.
records.description: Would require local jurisdiction to administratively approve an application to replace existing residential windows with California Energy Code-compliant windows

records.title: Low-income energy assistance.
records.description: Requires the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) to direct electrical and gas corporations to prioritize measurable improvements in household affordability when performing home weatherization services for low-income customers. Mandates whole-home improvements, coordinated delivery across different fuel types and housing situations, and program designs that benefit tenants in rental properties.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: advanced manufacturing facilities: exemption.
records.description:
Expands CEQA’s definition of “natural and protected lands” to include habitats for candidate, sensitive, or special-status species identified by state or federal agencies. 

Changes CEQA exemptions: adds location limits for day care center and family day care home exemptions (including restrictions related to industrial zoning and proximity to active oil and natural gas extraction/refining), and adds conditions to the advanced manufacturing exemption including community benefits agreements and labor requirements. 

Excludes tourism facilities from the HE rezoning exemption and repeals the prior exception that allowed oil and gas infrastructure in some rezoning cases.

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing element: interim housing units: acutely low income households.
records.description: Allows a city or county that has met or exceeded emergency shelter capacity and provides committed support for interim housing to report those interim units as approved or disapproved for acutely low‑income households in the HE APR, and directs HCD to let approved interim housing count for up to 50% of a jurisdiction’s share of regional need for acutely low‑income households

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing element: regional housing needs allocation: judicial review.
records.description: amends existing RHNA law by adding a provision that makes the final decisions made by councils of govts regarding RHNA subject to judicial review, meaning these decisions can be challenged in court.

records.title: Manufactured housing: classification as real property.
records.description: Aims to make it easier for manufactured homes, mobilehomes, and commercial modulars to be classified as real property, thereby facilitating financing and homeownership.

records.title: Prohousing enhanced infrastructure financing districts.
records.description: Would authorize eligible jurisdictions designated as prohousing to establish a prohousing enhanced infrastructure financing district. The bill would also require that the jurisdiction that established, and projects located within, a district receive enhanced points or preference than the baseline provided to other prohousing jurisdictions.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: railroad grade crossing closure.
records.description: Would make the closure of railroad grade crossings deemed a public safety threat by the Public Utilities Commission  CEQA exempt. Does not apply to high-speed rail projects.

records.title: Development projects: preliminary estimate of required improvements: onsite and offsite improvements.
records.description: Amends the Permit Streamlining Act for housing projects by allowing applicants to request a preliminary estimate of required onsite and offsite improvements when submitting a preliminary application or application.Local agency must deliver that estimate in 30 business days. Also requires agencies, within 30 business days of deeming a post-entitlement permit application complete, to provide an itemized list of all improvements required before permit issuance.

records.title: Mitigation Fee Act.
records.description: The Mitigation Fee Act governs how local agencies can establish, increase, or impose fees on development projects, ensuring there's a clear connection between the fee and the project's impact. Agencies must identify how the fee will be used and demonstrate its relevance to the project. Upon receiving these fees, they must also manage them as specified. This bill proposes additional requirements: any fee must be based on the actual impact on the need for public facilities and consider whether a development project involves removing or replacing existing uses. If so, agencies must provide a fee credit or reduce the fee in proportion to the impact of the eliminated or replaced use.

records.title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: relocation.
records.description: Would let CDFW issue a permit to relocate up to 10 WJTs from a parcel without requiring fees or other mitigation, provided the applicant submits a permit and meets conditions such as relocating each tree within 2.5 kilometers of its original location and following the department’s relocation guidelines and protocols.

records.title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: fees.
records.description: CDFW already must adjust WJT fees annually; this bill would additionally require CDFW to consider making fees proportional to project impact and using tiered fee levels by project type, size, or other criteria.

records.title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: life-sustaining services: take permit.
records.description: Amends existing WJTCA to allow the department to permit tree removal without fees if it supports essential services, such as maintenance or construction, provided the department is convinced of the necessity. The department must respond to permit requests within 30 days, or within 10 days for urgent health or safety threats. Once approved, permit holders have 60 days to carry out the removal, extendable at the department's discretion

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing development projects: subdivisions.
records.description:
1. Requires height limits for housing apply strictly to the physical height of a building, not the number of floors, and prohibits local agencies from imposing front or internal setbacks that would prevent the construction of the maximum number of allowed units based on minimum lot sizes. 
2. Revises criteria for ministerial approval of housing on certain subdivided lots, allowing for smaller newly created parcels in multifamily zones and adjusting the definition of "net habitable sqft" to exclude stairs and enclosed bicycle parking. 
3. Local agencies must now include specific data on housing projects approved under these new provisions in their annual reports to the state.

records.title: Accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units.
records.description: Existing law requires any impact fees charged for an ADU that has more than 750 sqft of interior livable space to be charged proportionately in relation to the square footage of the primary dwelling unit. This bill would additionally require the charge to be based only on the area in excess of 750 sqft of interior livable space.

records.title: Subdivision Map Act: tentative maps: expiration dates.
records.description: Would extend the expiration period for approved or conditionally approved tentative subdivision maps from 24 months to 8 years, with certain exceptions.

records.title: Accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units: electrical service connections.
records.description: Requires the CPUC to adopt by September 30, 2027 specific timelines for electrical corporations to respond to and process requests to energize ADUs and JADUs, and to require utilities to meet certain compliance requirements when implementing those timelines.

records.title: Zero- and near-zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles: incentives: transparency.
records.description: would require California agencies administering medium- and heavy-duty zero- and near-zero-emission vehicle incentive programs to use standardized pricing and transparency data as a condition for model eligibility, beginning January 1, 2027, and would strengthen oversight for voucher-based and other Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund and Low-Carbon Fuel Standard-linked programs.

records.title: Planning and Zoning Law: housing leadership designation.
records.description: Establishes a "housing leadership designation" for cities/counties that demonstrate exceptional housing production and proactive local policies to incentivize greater housing development and provide regulatory relief. To qualify, a jurisdiction must have submitted complete APRs for the past five years and meet specific housing production targets based on its affordability level. ( "affordable jurisdictions"-permit at least five units per 1,000 residents annually, "unaffordable jurisdictions" - 7.5 units, and "extremely unaffordable jurisdictions" -10 units)

records.title: Skilled and trained workforce requirements.
records.description: Would expand and strengthen California’s skilled and trained workforce requirements by adding notice, posting, reporting, penalty, and enforcement rules for public entities, private developers, contractors, and subcontractors.

records.title: Subdivision Map Act: action or proceeding.
records.description: Would bar certain lawsuits under the Subdivision Map Act when they raise substantially similar claims or issues to a CEQA action involving the same defendant, if specified conditions are met.

records.title: Streamlined housing approvals: hazardous waste sites.
records.description: Currently, developments cannot be built on hazardous waste sites unless cleared by health or environmental agencies. The new bill modifies this restriction by allowing development on such sites if specific actions are taken before the project is completed, such as obtaining a suitability determination from relevant agencies.
